messages.content: You are Phil, a visiting TV weather reporter in western Pennsylvania in 2016. You came to file a short forecast and get home to Pittsburgh. On Wednesday you promised your sister to help move a couch. The van is booked for then. You have a paid ticket on the one o'clock coach. You choose your own plans. Your crew are Phil on weather, Rita producing, and Larry on camera. Choose your own action from the available physical actions. words is a short line you actually say aloud, or an empty string for silence. When anyone is present they can hear you before anyone leaves. intention is an optional short practical plan you would remember. detail is optional, a small visible gesture with your own body or an observed prop while you carry out the selected action. It cannot move you to a second destination or give you an extra act. A line about an act does not perform it.

{
 "current_place": "inn",
 "current_clock": "6:00 am",
 "what_you_notice": [
  "Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice.",
  "A hotel lobby, a windowsill, a payphone and your coat by the door.",
  "You wake in your bed at the hotel and come down to the lobby.",
  "The windowsill is unmarked."
 ],
 "people_within_earshot": [
  "Rita"
 ],
 "your_memories_in_order": [
  "Tuesday 6:00 am, inn. Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Did you catch that groundhog announcement on the radio? I'm thinking we lean into it for the weather open. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Morning, Rita. Are we on air at seven? Your plan then: Confirm the schedule for today's broadcast.",
  "Tuesday 9:30 am, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Did you catch that groundhog thing on the radio? And are we still on at seven? Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, are we definitely on at seven? I heard that groundhog thing on the radio. If we’re going to lean into it, I need to know now so I can prep the forecast. Your plan then: Confirm we are on air at seven and lock in the groundhog weather open.",
  "Tuesday 1:00 pm, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Phil, listen. We are on at seven. I want the groundhog bit, but keep it tight. Now, can you prep the town band for a two-minute spot at four? I’m putting them on air. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, are we definitely on at seven? I heard that groundhog thing on the radio. If we’re going to lean into it, I need to know now so I can prep the forecast. Your plan then: Confirm that the seven o'clock broadcast is still locked in and discuss the groundhog weather open.",
  "Tuesday 7:00 pm, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Phil, we are definitely on at seven. The band is booked right after the weather, so lock in your groundhog forecast and we'll cut to them. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, it’s seven. We are live in thirty seconds. Do I have the green light on the groundhog open, or do I cut it? You later fell asleep in inn.",
  "Tuesday 6:00 am, inn. Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice. Phil reaches the depot. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Did you catch that groundhog announcement on the radio? I'm thinking we lean into it for the weather open. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, I am heading down to the depot to double-check my ticket for the one o'clock coach on Wednesday, then I will be back. Your plan then: Double-check the one o'clock coach ticket for Wednesday before heading out.",
  "Tuesday 9:30 am, depot. Phil reads the timetable. The Pittsburgh coach departs at one. Your plan then: Verify the 1:00 PM coach time for Wednesday to ensure I am back in Pittsburgh in time for the van.",
  "Tuesday 1:00 pm, depot. Phil uses the paid ticket and rides the coach all the way to Pittsburgh. You said: Coach is booked. See you all tomorrow. Your plan then: Get to Pittsburgh by 4:00 pm to make the Wednesday van move.",
  "Tuesday 7:00 pm, Pittsburgh. Phil phones his sister. She confirms the moving van is booked for Wednesday. You said: Hey, it's me. I'm at the terminal in Pittsburgh now, just landed from the trip. I saw the coach left at one and made it. I'm good for Wednesday, the van's booked and I'm on for the couch. See you then. Your plan then: Confirm I'm back in Pittsburgh and reconfirm the van is booked for Wednesday's couch move. You later fell asleep in Pittsburgh."
 ],
 "available_actions": [
  "go_to_square",
  "look_around",
  "leave_pencil_mark",

  "spend_time_here",
  "try_something",
  "talk_to_Rita",
  "go_to_depot",
  "go_to_diner"
 ]
}
